syntheses.title: End-to-End CNN Steering vs. Mid-Level RNN Trajectory Prediction Approaches
syntheses.body: There is a contradiction between the approach of using a CNN that learns the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile (claim e66d15a0-9347-5814-b053-1ff1dea8058d) and the approach of using ChauffeurNet, an RNN that takes mid-level input and outputs driving trajectories for control (claim cc49c2d4-b50d-5322-8525-304268249b24). The disagreement lies in the level of abstraction and input representation used: the CNN approach operates end-to-end from raw sensor data to control commands, while the RNN approach relies on mid-level representations and predicts trajectories rather than direct control commands. This reflects differing methodologies in autonomous driving system design, with implications for training, interpretability, and robustness.

syntheses.title: Effectiveness of Pure Imitation Learning in Autonomous Driving
syntheses.body: There is a contradiction regarding the effectiveness of pure imitation learning for autonomous driving. One claim states that pure imitation learning is insufficient even with 30 million examples and mid-level input/output representations (claim 639f88c8-001d-587a-bae9-390fb3c89dcf), supported by findings of model failures such as getting stuck or colliding with parked vehicles despite viable passing options (claim cf5a09ec-bfde-5049-ac07-ec7d2e843d78). Conversely, another claim highlights that this work advances capabilities using purely offline data without reinforcement learning (claim 00b87cf9-68f9-5906-a053-5253e3f2a9e5), suggesting progress in imitation learning approaches. The contradiction centers on whether pure imitation learning alone is sufficient for reliable autonomous driving performance.

syntheses.title: Reliability of End-to-End Trained Networks for Autonomous Driving
syntheses.body: There is a contradiction between claims about the reliability of end-to-end trained networks for autonomous driving. ALVINN demonstrated that an end-to-end trained neural network can steer a car on public roads (claim 443f6210-6468-59f8-8167-b719d39fc8fd), and the system is vehicle-make and model independent (claim 34d85362-1ab7-5462-ac7c-f2c84434250b). However, DAVE's performance, which also used end-to-end training on human driving data, was not reliable enough to replace modular off-road driving approaches (claim dd51b232-3e92-5d5e-b0e7-b982c3ee1e65). The contradiction concerns the reliability and generalizability of end-to-end networks across different driving contexts and vehicle platforms.
